document_title: Code of Ethics and Standards of Practice (2026 edition)
notes: One of the oldest professional ethics codes (adopted 1913, continuously updated). 2026 edition includes anti-harassment provisions tied to protected class status. Mandatory ethics training every 3 years. Enforcement through local/state REALTOR® boards with complaint and arbitration system. Membership revocation for violations.

First adopted 1959 (first Canadian real estate ethics code). Based on moral integrity, competent service, and dedication to public welfare. Requires written disclosure of agency relationships and conflicts of interest. Binding on all CREA members as condition of membership.

Administered through state/territory Real Estate Institute affiliates. Underpins training programs, codes of conduct, and awards programs. As Australian FIABCI chapter, REIA also applies FIABCI International Code of Ethics. Requires acting in client's best interests, ethical/fair/honest dealing, and protection of public against fraud.

Global ethics framework for real estate professionals. All members must agree to respect the FIABCI Code upon joining. FIABCI is a member of the International Ethics Standards Coalition and signatory to UN Global Compact 10 Principles. Member country associations (including REIA, NAR, CREA) align with this framework.

Effective February 2022, replacing prior Rules of Conduct for Members, Rules of Conduct for Firms, and Global Ethical Principles. Principles: honesty, integrity, competence, service, respect, responsibility. Mandatory CPD for chartered status. Peer review and disciplinary proceedings for violations. Also applies to Section F (construction surveying).

Founded 1933; one of the oldest property management ethics codes. Covers fiduciary duty, loyalty to client, non-commingling of funds, prohibition on material misrepresentation of client assets. Enforced by Ethics and Discipline Committee; membership or designation revocation for violations.

Corporate-level code for firms holding AMO accreditation. Covers fiduciary duties, non-commingling of client funds, avoidance of conflicts of interest, prohibition on material rebates/gifts. Accreditation revocation or letter of censure for violations. Stringently enforced by IREM.

organization: National Association of Residential Property Managers
document_title: Code of Ethics and Standards of Professionalism
notes: Adopted 1994, amended multiple times. Covers duty to public, non-discrimination, fiduciary responsibility, confidentiality, fair housing compliance. Mandatory ethics course every 4 years. FTC (2014) required elimination of competition-limiting provisions.

Organized around Canons including unbiased analysis, public protection, and non-detrimental conduct toward profession. Enforced through Peer Review Proceedings (Regulation No. 6). Designation revocation for violations. Updated May 2022; 2025 version also available.

document_title: Principles of Appraisal Practice and Code of Ethics
notes: All members must subscribe. Covers honesty, impartiality, competency over financial gain, confidentiality, conflict avoidance, and five-year record retention. Formal written complaint process. Covers real estate, personal property, business valuation, and machinery/equipment appraisers.

document_title: USPAP Ethics Rule (within Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice)
notes: USPAP Ethics Rule is legally required for all licensed/certified appraisers in all US states. Three sections: Conduct, Management, Confidentiality. Prohibits predetermined value opinions in exchange for compensation. 2024 edition expanded non-discrimination obligations. Enforcement via state licensing boards. Most legally enforceable ethics framework in real estate.

Requires honesty, professional conduct, transparent communication, honest advertising, and non-circumvention of industry standards. NAMB L.I.S.A. (Lending Integrity Seal of Approval) augments enforcement with continuing education, criminal background check, and ethics grievance review process.

National MBA has Code of Conduct; state affiliates maintain Canons of Ethics. Covers non-discrimination, candor and fairness, timely loan processing, integrity of loan submissions, and confidentiality. Principles enforced at state/local association level.

document_title: Code of Ethics and Standards of Practice
notes: Ethics course required as part of CCIM designation curriculum. For REALTOR® members, processed through NAR Code of Ethics system. Non-REALTORS® subject to direct CCIM discipline. Covers commercial real estate investment and brokerage professionals.

organization: Society of Industrial and Office Realtors
document_title: Code of Ethical Principles and Standards of Professional Practice
profession_name: Industrial and Office Real Estate Specialist
notes: Approved 1998, effective 1999. Substantially consistent with NAR Code but adapted for commercial real estate. Includes USPAP compliance for appraisal activities and IREM Code compliance for property management activities. Governed by SIOR Ethics and Arbitration Procedures Manual; designation revocation for violations.
